items.example: Tides scour the lagoon mouth.
items.exampleCN: 潮水冲刷着潟湖口。

items.example: Seagrass covers the lagoon floor.
items.exampleCN: 海草覆盖着潟湖底。

items.meaning: a ridge of sand built by waves
items.example: A sandbar seals the lagoon in summer.
items.exampleCN: 夏季沙坝封住潟湖。

items.example: The estuary opens freely to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 河口自由地向海敞开。

definition_zh: 海洋生态系统（海洋生物群落与其物理环境相互作用构成的整体）
definition_en: the community of marine organisms together with the physical environment they interact with
core_image: 从水面透下的光、随流漂动的浮游生物、吃它们的鱼、再把养分还给水的细菌，连成一台不停运转的机器
scene: 研究员把海草床、鱼群与水流放在同一张图表上分析。The marine ecosystem depends on tiny plankton at its base.
sceneCN: 这里 marine ecosystem 指「海洋生物群落与环境构成的整体系统」（第 1 个义项：作为功能整体）；句意为海洋生态系统依靠最底层的微小浮游生物支撑。

pos.zh: 海洋生态系统（可数，复数 marine ecosystems）

derivatives.zh: marinus（拉丁「海的」）→ 海洋的：与海有关的
eco-（希腊 oikos「住所」）+ system（希腊 systema「组合体」）→ 生态系统：生物群落与环境构成的整体
eco-（oikos「住所」）+ -logy（学科后缀）→ 生态学：研究生物与环境关系的学科
ecology + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 生态的：属于生态学或生态关系的
ecology + -ist（从业者后缀）→ 生态学家：研究生态关系的人

senses.title: The system as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的海洋生态系统
senses.definition: the living community and its physical setting taken as one functioning unit
senses.definitionCN: 把生物群落与物理环境当作一个运作单位
senses.example: The marine ecosystem depends on tiny plankton at its base.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生态系统依靠最底层的微小浮游生物支撑。
senses.why: ecosystem already means a community plus its environment, and marine narrows it to the sea.
senses.whyCN: ecosystem 本义就是群落加环境，marine 把它收窄到海洋。

senses.title: The producer layer
senses.titleCN: 生产者层：浮游植物与海藻
senses.definition: the photosynthetic organisms that capture energy at the base
senses.definitionCN: 在底层捕获能量的光合生物
senses.example: Phytoplankton drive the marine ecosystem's energy supply.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游植物驱动海洋生态系统的能量供给。
senses.why: every ecosystem needs an entry point for energy, and in the sea that point is mostly single-celled photosynthesis.
senses.whyCN: 每个生态系统都需要能量入口，在海里这个入口主要是单细胞光合作用。

senses.title: The consumer food web
senses.definition: the network of animals that eat producers and one another
senses.definitionCN: 以生产者及其他动物为食的动物网络
senses.example: Overfishing reshapes the marine ecosystem's food web.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞改变了海洋生态系统的食物网。
senses.why: energy captured by producers passes through a branching chain of eaters, which is what the word ecosystem treats as its wiring.
senses.whyCN: 生产者捕获的能量经过分叉的取食链传递，这正是生态系统一词当作线路的部分。

senses.title: Decomposers and nutrient cycling
senses.definition: the organisms and processes that return nutrients to the water
senses.definitionCN: 把养分送回水中的生物与过程
senses.example: Bacteria recycle nutrients throughout the marine ecosystem.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在整个海洋生态系统中循环养分。
senses.why: a system must close its loops, and decomposition is the return path that keeps nutrients available.
senses.whyCN: 系统必须闭合回路，分解就是让养分持续可用的返回路径。

senses.title: The physical environment
senses.definition: light, temperature, salinity, pressure and currents as the setting of life
senses.definitionCN: 作为生命环境的光、温度、盐度、压力与水流
senses.example: Light limits the marine ecosystem in deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 在深水中，光限制着海洋生态系统。
senses.why: the non-living half of the definition is real: without the physical setting there is no system to speak of.
senses.whyCN: 定义中非生命的那一半是实指的：没有物理环境就谈不上系统。

senses.title: A named type by setting
senses.definition: a particular system such as a coastal, open-ocean, deep-sea or vent ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 沿岸、开阔海、深海或喷口等具体类型的系统
senses.example: The vent marine ecosystem runs on chemistry, not sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 喷口海洋生态系统靠化学而非阳光运转。
senses.why: the same definition applies at different scales, so the phrase multiplies into named types.
senses.whyCN: 同一定义适用于不同尺度，因此这个短语分化出多种命名类型。

senses.title: A unit of services and impact
senses.definition: the system valued for fisheries, carbon storage and waste processing
senses.definitionCN: 从渔业、碳储存与废物处理角度被估值的系统
senses.example: The marine ecosystem provides food for billions of people.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生态系统为数十亿人提供食物。
senses.why: policy needs a countable unit, so the ecosystem becomes the thing that supplies services and absorbs damage.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要可计数的单位，于是生态系统成为提供服务、承受损害的对象。

senses.title: A model and monitoring unit
senses.definition: the system represented in equations and tracked by indicators
senses.definitionCN: 用方程表示、用指标追踪的系统
senses.example: The model simplifies the marine ecosystem into a few dozen groups.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把海洋生态系统简化成几十个类群。
senses.why: to predict change, scientists must turn the whole into variables, so the word also names the modelled object.
senses.whyCN: 为了预测变化，科学家必须把整体化为变量，因此这个词也命名被建模的对象。

intro.en: Marine ecosystem joins a Latin adjective to a twentieth-century coinage. Marine comes from mare 'sea' through marinus. Ecosystem was coined in 1935 from Greek oikos 'household' plus systema 'organised whole'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine ecosystem 把拉丁形容词接在一个二十世纪新造词上。marine 经 marinus 来自 mare「海」。ecosystem 一九三五年以希腊 oikos「家宅」加 systema「有组织的整体」造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', the source of English marine and maritime.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，是英语 marine 与 maritime 的来源。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household' and supplied the eco- of ecology and ecosystem.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家宅」，提供 ecology 与 ecosystem 的 eco-。

items.en: Systema meant an organised whole made of parts, and gave English system.
items.cn: systema 意为由部分组成的有组织整体，给出英语 system。

items.en: The botanist Arthur Tansley coined ecosystem for the physical system formed by organisms and their environment.
items.cn: 植物学家坦斯利造出 ecosystem 一词，指生物与其环境构成的物理系统。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century oceanography and fisheries science combined the two words into a standard term.
items.cn: 二十世纪中期的海洋学与渔业科学把两个词组合成标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the phrase's earliest technical use is not consistently dated, though each element is well documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个短语最早的技术使用各家年代不一，尽管每个成分记载清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the scientific terms most easily swapped for marine ecosystem; group two holds the ecological units that sit at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易与海洋生态系统互换的科学术语；第二组是不同尺度上的生态单位。

entries.definition: The science that studies marine ecosystems; it is a discipline, while the ecosystem is what the discipline examines.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生态系统的学科；它是一门学问，而生态系统是被研究的对象。

entries.definition: A particular place where organisms live, such as a reef or a vent; it is a component of an ecosystem, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生活的特定地点，如礁或喷口；它是生态系统的组成部分，而非整体。

entries.definition: All the organisms living together in a place; it excludes the physical environment that ecosystem includes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一地点共同生活的全部生物；不含生态系统所包括的物理环境。

entries.definition: A near-synonym stressing the open ocean as a body of water; marine is the broader technical modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，强调开阔海洋这一水体；marine 是更宽的技术限定词。

entries.definition: The general unit of organisms plus environment; it may be forest, lake or city.
entries.definitionCN: 生物加环境的一般单位；可以是森林、湖泊或城市。

entries.definition: A large regional community defined by climate, such as tundra or rainforest; it is far larger than one marine ecosystem.
entries.definitionCN: 由气候定义的大型区域群落，如苔原或雨林；比单个海洋生态系统大得多。

entries.definition: The network of who eats whom; it is one part of an ecosystem's structure.
entries.definitionCN: 谁吃谁的网络；它是生态系统结构的一部分。

entries.definition: The living organisms of a region taken together; it excludes water, light and temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区的全部生物；不含水、光与温度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin roots and real ecological levels, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁词根以及真实的生态层级，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: eco- is oikos, a household: an ecosystem is a household of living things plus its house.
normal.cn: eco- 即 oikos「家宅」：生态系统就是生物的家户加上它的房子。

normal.en: marine is mare, the sea: the phrase simply puts the household in the sea.
normal.cn: marine 即 mare「海」：这个短语只是把这个家户放进海里。

normal.en: Four parts to remember: producers, consumers, decomposers, physical setting.
normal.cn: 记四部分：生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境。

normal.en: Energy enters as sunlight or chemicals and leaves as heat; matter goes round in loops.
normal.cn: 能量以阳光或化学物进入、以热离开；物质则在圈里循环。

normal.en: Policy phrases mark the unit: ecosystem health, ecosystem services, ecosystem management.
normal.cn: 政策短语标出这个单位：生态系统健康、生态系统服务、生态系统管理。

abstract.en: A marine ecosystem is a city whose citizens never agreed on a plan.
abstract.cn: 海洋生态系统是一座市民从未商定计划的城。

abstract.en: It is a ledger where sunlight is deposited and heat is withdrawn.
abstract.cn: 它是一本账，存入阳光，取出热量。

abstract.en: The sea keeps its economy invisible; we see only the bankruptcies.
abstract.cn: 海把自己的经济藏起来；我们只看见破产。

examples.en: Nutrient runoff can collapse a coastal marine ecosystem.
examples.cn: 养分径流可能使一个沿岸海洋生态系统崩溃。

examples.en: The marine ecosystem of the shelf supports most commercial fishing.
examples.cn: 大陆架的海洋生态系统支撑着大部分商业捕捞。

examples.en: Scientists model the marine ecosystem to predict fish stocks.
examples.cn: 科学家为预测鱼类资源而建立海洋生态系统模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: marine（海的）+ ecosystem（生态系统）＝海洋里的生物群落加环境；记四部分：生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境。

root: marine（拉丁 mare「海」→ marinus）+ ecosystem（希腊 oikos「家宅」+ systema「整体」，一九三五年造词）；短语为二十世纪海洋科学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one working system: the whole, its producers, its consumers, its decomposers, its physical setting, its named types, its services and its modelled form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个运作系统展开：整体、生产者、消费者、分解者、物理环境、命名类型、服务，以及被建模的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight entering water, plankton capturing it, fish eating plankton, bacteria returning the nutrients.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光进入水中，浮游生物捕获它，鱼吃浮游生物，细菌把养分送回。

branches.en: WHOLE AND SETTING: the system, then the water, light and heat that frame it.
branches.cn: 整体与环境：先是系统，再是框住它的水、光与热。

branches.en: PRODUCERS: the entry point where energy becomes food.
branches.cn: 生产者：能量变成食物的入口。

branches.en: EATING AND RETURNING: the food web, then decomposition closing the loop.
branches.cn: 取食与归还：先是食物网，再是闭合回路的分解。

branches.en: TYPES AND MODELS: real named systems, then the same systems in equations.
branches.cn: 类型与模型：先是真实的命名系统，再是方程中的同一系统。

branches.en: SERVICES: the system counted as food, carbon store and waste processor.
branches.cn: 服务：把系统计为食物、碳库与废物处理者。

intro.en: Marine ecosystem is a two-word technical phrase: a Latin-derived adjective plus a Greek-derived noun, each with a productive family.
intro.cn: marine ecosystem 是两词技术短语：拉丁语源形容词加希腊语源名词，各自都有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: Mare supplies marine; oikos and systema are Greek and have no Latin cognates, though Latin borrowed Greek systema as systema.
latinIntro.cn: mare 提供 marine；oikos 与 systema 属希腊语，在拉丁语中无同族词，尽管拉丁语曾借入希腊 systema 作 systema。

items.example: Mare gave marinus and marine.
items.exampleCN: mare 给出 marinus 与 marine。

items.example: Marinus is the source of marine.
items.exampleCN: marinus 是 marine 的来源。

items.example: Marine species fill the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 海洋物种充满大陆架。

items.example: Oikos is the root of ecology.
items.exampleCN: oikos 是 ecology 的词根。

items.example: Systema became English system.
items.exampleCN: systema 变成英语 system。

items.example: The reef is one ecosystem.
items.exampleCN: 这座礁是一个生态系统。

items.meaning: the study of organisms and environment
items.meaningCN: 研究生物与环境的学科
items.example: Ecology grew out of natural history.
items.exampleCN: 生态学由博物学发展而来。

items.example: The shelf marine ecosystem is highly productive.
items.exampleCN: 陆架海洋生态系统生产力很高。

items.meaning: a feeding position in a food web
items.meaningCN: 食物网中的一个营养位置
items.example: Each trophic level loses most of its energy.
items.exampleCN: 每个营养级都会损失大部分能量。

definition_zh: 海洋生物（生活在海洋中的任何生物个体或类群）
definition_en: any living thing that spends all or part of its life in the sea
core_image: 一只小小的甲壳类在咸水里张合附肢，身体里的盐分与周围海水不断交换
scene: 取样瓶里的一只小甲壳类在低温海水中仍缓慢活动。A marine organism must cope with salt, cold and constant pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 marine organism 指「生活在海洋中的生物个体」（第 1 个义项：作为个体或类群的海洋生物）；句意为一种海洋生物必须应对盐分、低温与持续压力。

pos.zh: 海洋生物（可数，复数 marine organisms）

derivatives.zh: marinus（拉丁「海的」）→ 海洋的：与海有关的
organon（希腊「工具、器官」）+ -ismos（名词后缀）→ 生物体：由器官构成的有机整体
micro-（希腊「小」）+ organism（生物体）→ 微生物：肉眼不可见的生物
organon（器官）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ 有机的：与生命器官有关的
organon（希腊「工具、器官」经拉丁 organum 借入）→ 器官；机构

senses.title: Any sea-living thing
senses.titleCN: 海洋生物：生活在海中的任何生物
senses.definition: any organism whose habitat is the sea
senses.definitionCN: 以海洋为栖息环境的任何生物
senses.example: A marine organism must cope with salt, cold and constant pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 一种海洋生物必须应对盐分、低温与持续压力。
senses.why: marine fixes the habitat and organism fixes the living thing, so the phrase covers every sea-dwelling species.
senses.whyCN: marine 限定栖息地，organism 限定生物本身，短语因此涵盖所有海生物种。

senses.title: The planktonic kind
senses.definition: a small organism that drifts with currents rather than swimming against them
senses.definitionCN: 随水流漂移、不主动逆流游泳的小型生物
senses.example: A drifting marine organism cannot choose its water.
senses.exampleCN: 漂浮的海洋生物无法选择自己所在的水。
senses.why: most marine organisms are too small or too weak to swim far, so drifting becomes a defining lifestyle.
senses.whyCN: 多数海洋生物太小或太弱，无法远游，因此漂移成为决定性的生活方式。

senses.title: The bottom-living kind
senses.definition: an organism attached to or crawling on the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 附着于或爬行于海底的生物
senses.example: A bottom-dwelling marine organism may never leave the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 底栖的海洋生物可能一生不离开岩石。
senses.why: the seafloor is a distinct habitat, so the phrase often names organisms defined by that attachment.
senses.whyCN: 海底是一种独立栖息地，因此这个短语常命名由附着方式定义的生物。

senses.title: The swimming kind
senses.definition: an organism strong enough to move against currents
senses.definitionCN: 有足够力量逆流移动的生物
senses.example: A fast marine organism such as a fish can cross the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 像鱼这样快速的海洋生物能横穿海盆。
senses.why: active movement changes how an organism feeds and migrates, so swimming is treated as a separate category.
senses.whyCN: 主动移动改变取食与迁徙方式，因此游泳被视作单独一类。

senses.title: A set of physiological adaptations
senses.titleCN: 生理适应：渗透、压力与温度
senses.definition: the organism considered for how it handles salinity, pressure and cold
senses.definitionCN: 从它如何应对盐度、压力与低温来考虑的生物
senses.example: Every marine organism regulates water and salt across its membranes.
senses.exampleCN: 每种海洋生物都要跨膜调节水与盐。
senses.why: seawater constantly pulls water across membranes, so survival depends on the adaptations the word implies.
senses.whyCN: 海水不断把水拉过膜，因此生存取决于这个词所隐含的适应。

senses.title: A member of a taxonomic group
senses.definition: the organism placed in a group such as bacteria, algae, invertebrates or vertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 被归入细菌、藻类、无脊椎动物或脊椎动物等类群的生物
senses.example: A marine organism may be single-celled or a whale.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物可以是单细胞，也可以是鲸。
senses.why: the phrase cuts across taxonomy, so its content is defined by habitat rather than by relatedness.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语横跨分类系统，因此其内容由栖息地而非亲缘关系决定。

senses.title: An ecological role
senses.titleCN: 生态角色：生产者、消费者、分解者
senses.definition: the organism considered by what it contributes to the food web
senses.definitionCN: 从它对食物网的贡献来考虑的生物
senses.example: A marine organism can be producer, grazer or decomposer.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物可以是生产者、摄食者或分解者。
senses.why: ecology needs roles, not names, so the phrase often stands for a function in a system.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要角色而非名字，因此这个短语常代表系统中的一种功能。

senses.title: A specimen for study
senses.definition: the organism collected, cultured or observed as a specimen
senses.definitionCN: 被采集、培养或观察作为样本的生物
senses.example: The marine organism survived three days in the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 这种海洋生物在水槽中存活了三天。
senses.why: laboratory work turns the category into a countable specimen, which is the sense most experiments use.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作把这个类别变成可计数的样本，这是多数实验使用的义项。

intro.en: Marine organism joins a Latin adjective to a Greek-derived noun. Marine goes back to mare 'sea' through marinus; organism goes back to Greek organon 'tool, organ' plus the noun ending -ismos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine organism 把拉丁形容词接在希腊语源名词上。marine 经 marinus 上溯 mare「海」；organism 上溯希腊 organon「工具、器官」加名词后缀 -ismos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' yielded marinus 'of the sea', which became English marine.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，后者成为英语 marine。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument, organ of the body'; Latin borrowed it as organum.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具、身体器官」；拉丁语借入作 organum。

items.en: The noun organism was formed in English in the eighteenth century from organ plus -ism, meaning an organised living body.
items.cn: 名词 organism 于十八世纪在英语中由 organ 加 -ism 构成，指有组织的活的躯体。

items.en: As biology professionalised, organism became the standard word for any living individual.
items.cn: 随着生物学专业化，organism 成为任何活个体的标准词。

items.en: Oceanography combined the two words to name any sea-dwelling living thing, from bacteria to whales.
items.cn: 海洋学把两个词组合，命名从细菌到鲸的任何海生生物。

items.en: Source uncertain (derivation detail only): the exact sense path from organon 'tool' to organism 'living body' is not fully documented in English sources, though the morphemes are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅派生细节存疑）：从 organon「工具」到 organism「活体」的具体语义路径在英语文献中记载不全，尽管语素本身可靠。

note.en: Group one holds the phrases most often used in place of marine organism; group two holds the general biological words.
note.cn: 第一组是常被用来替代 marine organism 的短语；第二组是泛指生物的词语。

entries.definition: A category of related organisms; one marine organism is an individual of a species.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关生物；一个海洋生物是某一物种的个体。

entries.definition: All sea-dwelling living things taken together; it is a mass term and cannot be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 全部海生生物的集合；是集合名词，不可计数。

entries.definition: The scientific study of marine organisms; it is a field, not a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物的科学；是一个学科，不是生物。

entries.definition: An organism too small to see with the naked eye; it may be marine or not.
entries.definitionCN: 肉眼不可见的生物；可以是海洋的，也可以不是。

entries.definition: Any living individual; it needs a qualifier to say where it lives.
entries.definitionCN: 任何活的个体；需要限定词才能说明生活在哪里。

entries.definition: A general word for a living being, usually an animal; it is informal and rarely used for bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生物，通常指动物；较口语，很少用于细菌。

entries.definition: A group capable of interbreeding; it is a category, while an organism is a member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 能相互繁殖的一群生物；它是类别，而个体是该类别的成员。

entries.definition: The drifting organisms of the water column; it is only one subset of marine organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 水柱中漂移的生物；只是海洋生物的一个子集。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin roots, real habitats and real lifestyles, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁词根、真实栖息地与生活方式，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: marine is mare, the sea; organism is a body built of organs: a body in the sea.
normal.cn: marine 是 mare「海」；organism 是由器官构成的躯体：海里的躯体。

normal.en: Three lifestyles divide the group: drifting, bottom-living, swimming.
normal.cn: 三种生活方式划分这一类：漂移、底栖、游泳。

normal.en: Salinity is the constant problem: water wants to leave or enter the body.
normal.cn: 盐度是恒久的问题：水总想离开或进入身体。

normal.en: Pressure rises one atmosphere for every ten metres, which is why deep organisms differ.
normal.cn: 每深十米压力增加一个大气压，因此深水生物与众不同。

normal.en: The phrase crosses taxonomy: a bacterium and a whale are both marine organisms.
normal.cn: 这个短语横跨分类：细菌与鲸都是海洋生物。

abstract.en: A marine organism is a negotiation with salt that never ends.
abstract.cn: 海洋生物是一场与盐永不结束的谈判。

abstract.en: It is a small pocket of fresh chemistry refusing to become seawater.
abstract.cn: 它是一小袋不肯变成海水的化学。

abstract.en: Every sea creature carries its own weather inside a membrane.
abstract.cn: 每个海生生物都在一层膜里带着自己的天气。

examples.en: The survey counted every marine organism larger than a millimetre.
examples.cn: 这次调查统计了所有大于一毫米的海洋生物。

examples.en: A marine organism may be a drifting larva for weeks before settling.
examples.cn: 一种海洋生物可能在漂浮幼体阶段待上数周才定居。

examples.en: The aquarium keeps each marine organism in filtered seawater.
examples.cn: 水族馆把每种海洋生物养在过滤海水中。

dict_mnemonic.text: marine（海的）+ organism（生物体）＝海洋生物；三种生活方式记漂浮、底栖、游泳，核心难题是盐与压力。

root: marine（拉丁 mare「海」→ marinus）+ organism（希腊 organon「工具、器官」+ -ismos）；短语为近代海洋科学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one living thing in salt water: the general category, three lifestyles, its physiology, its taxonomy, its ecological role and its use as a specimen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿咸水中的一个活物展开：总类别、三种生活方式、生理、分类、生态角色，以及作为样本的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body in salt water, constantly trading water and ions across its skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：咸水中的一个小躯体，不断隔着皮肤交换水与离子。

branches.en: CATEGORY AND TAXONOMY: any sea dweller, then its place in a classification.
branches.cn: 类别与分类：先是任何海生者，再是它在分类中的位置。

branches.en: THREE LIFESTYLES: drifting, bottom-living, swimming.
branches.cn: 三种生活方式：漂移、底栖、游泳。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: salt, cold and pressure shape the body.
branches.cn: 生理：盐、低温与压力塑造身体。

branches.en: ROLE: producer, grazer or decomposer in the food web.
branches.cn: 角色：食物网中的生产者、摄食者或分解者。

branches.en: SPECIMEN: the category becomes a countable object of study.
branches.cn: 样本：类别变成可计数的研究对象。

intro.en: Marine organism joins a Latin adjective and a Greek-derived noun, both of which read clearly morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: marine organism 把拉丁形容词与希腊语源名词组合，两者都能按语素清楚读出。

latinIntro.en: Mare provides the Latin entry. Organon is Greek; Latin organum is a borrowing from Greek, not a native cognate, so it is not listed.
latinIntro.cn: mare 提供拉丁条目。organon 属希腊语；拉丁 organum 是从希腊语借入，并非本土同族词，因此不列入。

items.example: Mare gives marinus and marine.
items.exampleCN: mare 给出 marinus 与 marine。

items.example: Marinus became English marine.
items.exampleCN: marinus 变成英语 marine。

items.example: Marine animals drink little seawater.
items.exampleCN: 海洋动物很少喝海水。

items.example: Organon is the root of organism.
items.exampleCN: organon 是 organism 的词根。

items.example: One organism, one life.
items.exampleCN: 一个生物体，一条生命。

items.meaning: an organism too small to see
items.example: Microorganisms dominate the open sea.
items.exampleCN: 微生物主导着开阔海洋。

items.example: Each marine organism has a salinity strategy.
items.exampleCN: 每种海洋生物都有盐度策略。

items.example: Plankton forms the base of the food web.
items.exampleCN: 浮游生物构成食物网的基础。

items.example: Benthos covers the seafloor.
items.exampleCN: 底栖生物覆盖着海底。

items.example: Nekton crosses whole ocean basins.
items.exampleCN: 游泳生物能横穿整个海盆。

definition_zh: 水生生物（生活在水中，包括淡水与海水中的生物）
definition_en: a living thing that lives in water, whether fresh, brackish or marine
core_image: 池塘边的一只小甲壳类在水草间穿行，鳃片一开一合，从水里取氧
scene: 取样瓶里的一只小甲壳类在淡水与海水混合的水中仍能活动。Every aquatic organism needs dissolved oxygen to survive.
sceneCN: 这里 aquatic organism 指「生活在水中的生物」（第 1 个义项：涵盖淡水与海水的水生生物总称）；句意为每种水生生物都需要溶解氧才能生存。

pos.zh: 水生生物（可数，复数 aquatic organisms）

derivatives.zh: aqua（拉丁「水」）+ -aticus（形容词后缀）→ 水生的：生长或生活在水中的
aqua（水）+ -arium（场所后缀）→ 水族馆：养水生动植物的场所
aqua（水）+ cultura（栽培、养殖）→ 水产养殖：在水中养殖动植物
organon（希腊「器官」）+ -ismos → 生物体：有组织的活的躯体
aquatic（水生的）+ ecosystem（生态系统）→ 水生生态系统：水环境中的生物群落与环境整体

senses.title: Any water-dwelling organism
senses.titleCN: 水生生物总称：淡咸水皆可
senses.definition: an organism that lives in water of any salinity
senses.definitionCN: 生活在任何盐度水体中的生物
senses.example: Every aquatic organism needs dissolved oxygen to survive.
senses.exampleCN: 每种水生生物都需要溶解氧才能生存。
senses.why: aquatic means 'of water', not 'of the sea', so the phrase is wider than marine organism.
senses.whyCN: aquatic 意为「水的」，不是「海的」，因此这个短语比 marine organism 更宽。

senses.title: A freshwater organism
senses.titleCN: 淡水生物：河流、湖泊与湿地
senses.definition: an organism living in rivers, lakes, ponds or wetlands
senses.definitionCN: 生活在河流、湖泊、池塘或湿地的生物
senses.example: The aquatic organism in this pond never sees salt water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个池塘里的水生生物从未见过咸水。
senses.why: freshwater is the largest non-marine aquatic setting, so the phrase is often used where that contrast matters.
senses.whyCN: 淡水是最大的非海洋水环境，因此这个短语常用于需要这一对照的场合。

senses.title: A marine or brackish organism
senses.titleCN: 海水或半咸水中的水生生物
senses.definition: an organism living in seawater or in mixed estuarine water
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海水或河口混合水中的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism in the estuary must tolerate changing salt.
senses.exampleCN: 河口的水生生物必须忍受盐度变化。
senses.why: aquatic includes the sea, so the phrase also covers marine and estuarine life when the emphasis is on water rather than ocean.
senses.whyCN: aquatic 包含海洋，因此当强调水而非海洋时，这个短语也涵盖海生与河口生物。

senses.title: A lifestyle category
senses.titleCN: 生活方式类别：漂浮、底栖、游泳
senses.definition: the organism classified by how it occupies the water column or bottom
senses.definitionCN: 按它如何占据水柱或水底来分类的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism may drift, crawl or swim.
senses.exampleCN: 水生生物可以漂浮、爬行或游泳。
senses.why: water offers distinct zones, so aquatic organisms are often grouped by where and how they move.
senses.whyCN: 水提供不同的区域，因此水生生物常按所在位置与移动方式分组。

senses.title: Respiration and osmoregulation
senses.definition: the organism considered for gills, skin exchange and salt balance
senses.definitionCN: 从鳃、皮肤交换与盐分平衡来考虑的生物
senses.example: An aquatic organism uses gills or skin to take oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水生生物用鳃或皮肤摄取氧气。
senses.why: water holds far less oxygen than air, so breathing and salt balance are the defining physiological problems.
senses.whyCN: 水中的氧远少于空气，因此呼吸与盐分平衡是决定性的生理难题。

senses.title: A water-quality indicator
senses.definition: the organism used to judge pollution or oxygen conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断污染或溶氧状况的生物
senses.example: A sensitive aquatic organism disappears when the stream is polluted.
senses.exampleCN: 溪流受污染时，敏感的水生生物会消失。
senses.why: organisms tolerate pollution unequally, so their presence becomes a measurement of water quality.
senses.whyCN: 生物对污染的耐受程度不同，因此它们的有无成为水质的量度。

senses.title: A cultured or experimental subject
senses.definition: the organism bred in ponds or kept in tanks for study
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘养殖或在水槽中饲养供研究的生物
senses.example: The hatchery raises an aquatic organism for restocking.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场养殖一种水生生物用于补充种群。
senses.why: aquaculture and laboratories turn the category into stock and subject, which is how the phrase is used in practice.
senses.whyCN: 水产养殖与实验室把这个类别变成养殖对象与实验对象，这是实际用法。

senses.title: A conservation or invasion unit
senses.titleCN: 保护与入侵语境中的单元
senses.definition: the organism considered as a protected native or a spreading invader
senses.definitionCN: 作为受保护的本土种或扩散中的入侵种来考虑的生物
senses.example: An introduced aquatic organism can crowd out native species.
senses.exampleCN: 引入的水生生物可能排挤本土物种。
senses.why: management works species by species, so the general phrase becomes a unit in protection and invasion policy.
senses.whyCN: 管理按物种逐一进行，因此这个总称成为保护与入侵政策中的单位。

intro.en: Aquatic organism joins a Latin adjective to a Greek-derived noun. Aquatic comes from Latin aqua 'water' through aquaticus, borrowed into English via French aquatique. Organism comes from Greek organon 'organ'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aquatic organism 把拉丁形容词接在希腊语源名词上。aquatic 经拉丁 aquaticus 来自 aqua「水」，又经法语 aquatique 进入英语。organism 来自希腊 organon「器官」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aqua meant 'water' and supplies aquarium, aqueduct and aquatic.
items.cn: aqua 意为「水」，提供 aquarium、aqueduct 与 aquatic。

items.en: Aquaticus meant 'living or growing in water', formed from aqua with the adjectival ending -aticus.
items.cn: aquaticus 意为「在水中生活或生长的」，由 aqua 加形容词词尾 -aticus 构成。

items.en: French aquatique carried the adjective into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aquatique 于十五世纪把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument, organ'; organism was formed in English from organ plus -ism.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具、器官」；organism 在英语中由 organ 加 -ism 构成。

items.en: Modern biology and limnology combined the two words to name water-dwelling life without committing to fresh or salt.
items.cn: 近代生物学与湖沼学把两个词组合，命名水生生物而不限定淡水或海水。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact phrase is recent and its earliest technical citation varies between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个确切短语出现较晚，其最早技术书证各家不一。

note.en: Group one holds the phrases most often confused with aquatic organism; group two holds the general habitat words.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 aquatic organism 混淆的短语；第二组是泛指栖息环境的词。

entries.definition: An organism of the sea; it excludes freshwater life, which aquatic organism includes.
entries.definitionCN: 海洋中的生物；不含淡水生物，而 aquatic organism 包含。

entries.definition: A plant living in or on water; it is one kingdom, not all water-dwelling life.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水里或水面的植物；只是一个界，不是全部水生生物。

entries.definition: An animal living in water; it excludes algae and bacteria, which organism covers.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水中的动物；不含藻类与细菌，而 organism 涵盖。

entries.definition: The community plus its water environment; one organism is a member, not the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 群落加上水环境；一个生物只是成员，不是整个系统。

entries.definition: Any living body; it needs a qualifier such as aquatic or marine to place it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何活的躯体；需要 aquatic 或 marine 之类限定词来定位。

entries.definition: An organism restricted to fresh water; aquatic organism also covers brackish and marine life.
entries.definitionCN: 局限于淡水的生物；aquatic organism 也涵盖半咸水与海水生物。

entries.definition: The organisms living on or in the bottom; it is one zone, not the whole water column.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在水底或底内的生物；只是一个区域，不是整个水柱。

entries.definition: The drifting organisms of the water column; it excludes swimmers and bottom dwellers.
entries.definitionCN: 水柱中漂移的生物；不含游泳者与底栖者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real Greek root and real habitat divisions, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的希腊词根与真实的栖息地划分，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aqua is water, so aquatic covers pond and sea alike.
normal.cn: aqua 是水，因此 aquatic 同时涵盖池塘与海洋。

normal.en: marine is only the salty subset of aquatic, not a synonym.
normal.cn: marine 只是 aquatic 中咸水的那一部分，并非同义词。

normal.en: Three water zones: drifting, bottom, swimming, each with its own organisms.
normal.cn: 三个水区：漂浮、水底、游泳，各有自己的生物。

normal.en: Water holds little oxygen, so gills and skin do the work.
normal.cn: 水中氧少，因此靠鳃与皮肤工作。

normal.en: Sensitive species make living water-quality meters.
normal.cn: 敏感物种就是活的水质测量计。

abstract.en: An aquatic organism is a small private sea kept inside a membrane.
abstract.cn: 水生生物是一小片被膜围起来的私人海。

abstract.en: It breathes a medium that would drown us and calls it home.
abstract.cn: 它呼吸着会淹死我们的介质，并称之为家。

abstract.en: Water is both its weather and its architecture.
abstract.cn: 水既是它的天气，也是它的建筑。

examples.en: The lake survey recorded every aquatic organism in the shallows.
examples.cn: 湖泊调查记录了浅水区的每一种水生生物。

examples.en: An aquatic organism may tolerate both fresh and brackish water.
examples.cn: 一种水生生物可能同时耐受淡水与半咸水。

examples.en: The lab cultures an aquatic organism to test toxicity.
examples.cn: 实验室培养一种水生生物来测试毒性。

dict_mnemonic.text: aquatic（水的）+ organism（生物）＝水生生物；比 marine 更宽，淡水海水都算，靠鳃或皮肤取氧。

root: aquatic（拉丁 aqua「水」→ aquaticus）+ organism（希腊 organon「器官」+ -ismos）；短语为近代生物学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one water-dwelling body: the whole category, freshwater and marine cases, three lifestyles, its breathing and salt balance, its role as an indicator, its cultured form and its place in conservation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿水中一个躯体展开：总类别、淡水与海水情形、三种生活方式、呼吸与盐分平衡、指示作用、养殖形态，以及保护中的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body moving among water plants, taking oxygen through gills.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小躯体在水草间移动，用鳃取氧。

branches.en: ONE CATEGORY, THREE SALINITIES: any water, then fresh, then marine or brackish.
branches.cn: 一个类别，三种盐度：先是任何水，再是淡水，再是海水或半咸水。

branches.en: LIFESTYLES: drifting, bottom-living and swimming divide the water.
branches.cn: 生活方式：漂移、底栖与游泳划分水体。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: oxygen is scarce and salt must be managed.
branches.cn: 生理：氧稀少，盐必须管理。

branches.en: INDICATOR AND STOCK: the organism measures water quality and becomes cultured stock.
branches.cn: 指示与养殖：生物测量水质，也成为养殖对象。

branches.en: POLICY UNIT: native or invader, it is counted one species at a time.
branches.cn: 政策单位：无论本土或入侵，都按物种逐一计数。

intro.en: Aquatic organism joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Greek-derived noun; each half has a productive family in English.
intro.cn: aquatic organism 把拉丁语源形容词与希腊语源名词组合，两半在英语中都有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: Aqua and aquaticus are the Latin entries. Greek organon supplies organism, with no native Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: aqua 与 aquaticus 是拉丁条目。希腊 organon 提供 organism，在拉丁语中没有本土同族词。

items.exampleCN: aqua 是拉丁语的「水」。

items.example: Aquaticus became English aquatic.
items.exampleCN: aquaticus 变成英语 aquatic。

items.example: Aquatic plants fill the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 水生植物长满沼泽。

items.example: The aquarium holds local aquatic species.
items.exampleCN: 水族馆饲养本地水生种。

items.example: Aquaculture supplies half the seafood eaten.
items.exampleCN: 水产养殖提供所吃海鲜的一半。

items.example: Organon is the root of organism.
items.exampleCN: organon 是 organism 的词根。

items.example: A single organism can change a pond.
items.exampleCN: 一个生物体就能改变一座池塘。

items.example: The pond teems with aquatic organisms.
items.exampleCN: 池塘里满是水生生物。

items.example: Freshwater species cannot cross the strait.
items.exampleCN: 淡水物种无法越过海峡。

items.example: Marine organisms are a subset of aquatic ones.
items.exampleCN: 海洋生物是水生生物的一个子集。

definition_zh: 水下的；在水面以下地（指位置在水面之下，或在水下进行）
definition_en: located, happening or operating below the surface of water
core_image: 水面像一面天花板，光从上方漏下来，四周全是蓝色的水，人在下面抬头看
scene: 相机在昏暗的水下仍能拍到礁壁的细节。The camera works even in dim underwater conditions.
sceneCN: 这里 underwater 指「位于水面以下的」（第 1 个义项：描述位置在水面之下）；句意为这台相机即使在昏暗的水下环境里也能工作。

derivatives.zh: under（古英语 under「在下方」）→ 在……下面；在下方
water（古英语 wæter「水」）→ 水；浇水
under + sea（复合形容词）→ 海底的：位于海面之下的（多用于海床与海底资源）
sub-（拉丁「在下」）+ sea（海）→ 海底的：用于海底油气与工程设施
underwater（水下的）+ archaeology（考古学，希腊 arkhaiologia「古代研究」）→ 水下考古：研究淹没遗存的学科

senses.title: Below the water surface
senses.definition: situated beneath the surface of water
senses.definitionCN: 位于水面之下
senses.example: The camera works even in dim underwater conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机即使在昏暗的水下环境里也能工作。
senses.why: under supplies the position and water supplies the medium, so the compound is simply 'below water'.
senses.whyCN: under 提供位置，water 提供介质，复合词就是「在水之下」。

senses.title: The underwater environment
senses.definition: the conditions found below the surface, with dim light and rising pressure
senses.definitionCN: 水面之下的条件，光线昏暗、压力随深度上升
senses.example: Underwater visibility fell to two metres after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴之后水下能见度降到两米。
senses.why: once the word names a place, it also names the conditions that place imposes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词命名一个地点，它也就命名那个地点强加的条件。

senses.title: Activity carried out below water
senses.definition: work or movement done while submerged
senses.definitionCN: 在水下完成的工作或移动
senses.example: Welders repaired the hull underwater.
senses.exampleCN: 焊工在水下修补船体。
senses.why: the adverb use says how an action is done, not where an object sits.
senses.whyCN: 副词用法说明动作如何完成，而不是物体位于何处。

senses.title: Built structures below water
senses.definition: structures such as pipes, cables and tunnels placed below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 置于水面之下的管道、电缆与隧道等构筑物
senses.example: An underwater pipeline carries gas to the terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 一条水下管道把天然气输往终端。
senses.why: engineering needs a short modifier for anything installed below water, so the adjective attaches to the object.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要一个简短限定词来指任何安装在水下的东西，因此这个形容词附在物体上。

senses.title: Underwater imaging
senses.definition: photography or filming done beneath the surface
senses.definitionCN: 在水面之下进行的摄影或摄像
senses.example: Underwater footage showed the wreck in blue light.
senses.exampleCN: 水下影像在蓝光中显出沉船。
senses.why: cameras and lights must be sealed against water, so the compound marks a whole technical practice.
senses.whyCN: 相机与灯必须防水密封，因此这个复合词标出一整套技术实践。

senses.title: Below-water life
senses.definition: the living world considered as existing below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 被视为生活在水面之下的生命世界
senses.example: Underwater life depends on light reaching the shallows.
senses.exampleCN: 水下生命依赖到达浅水的光。
senses.why: the same position word can describe a habitat, which is how biology uses it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个位置词也能描述栖息环境，生物学正是这样使用。

senses.title: Financially below the surface
senses.titleCN: 财务上的「溺水」：资产低于负债
senses.definition: owing more on a property than it is worth
senses.definitionCN: 一处房产所欠的钱超过它的价值
senses.example: The family was underwater on their mortgage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人的房贷金额超过了房子价值。
senses.why: being below the surface is being unable to rise, which finance borrowed as a metaphor for negative equity.
senses.whyCN: 在水面之下意味着无法浮起，金融学借这个意象表示负资产。

senses.title: Submerged heritage
senses.definition: the archaeological record preserved beneath seas, lakes or rivers
senses.definitionCN: 保存在海、湖或河面之下的考古记录
senses.example: Underwater archaeology recovered amphorae from the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 水下考古从港湾中取出双耳瓶。
senses.why: water preserves some materials and hides them from looters, so a whole discipline takes the word as its name.
senses.whyCN: 水保存某些材料，也把它们藏起来不被盗掘，因此一整个学科用这个词命名。

intro.en: Underwater is a native English compound of under and water, both Old English words of Germanic origin. It has no Latin ancestry. The compound is recorded from the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: underwater 是英语本族复合词，由 under 与 water 构成，两者都是日耳曼语源的古英语词。它没有拉丁语祖先。复合词自十七世纪有记载。年代均为约数。

items.en: Under meant 'beneath, below' and descends from a Germanic preposition of the same sense.
items.cn: under 意为「在下方、低于」，来自同义的日耳曼语介词。

items.en: Wæter meant 'water' and is related to German Wasser and Dutch water.
items.cn: wæter 意为「水」，与德语 Wasser、荷兰语 water 同源。

items.en: Underwater appears in the seventeenth century, first as an adverb and adjective describing position below the surface.
items.cn: underwater 于十七世纪出现，最初作副词与形容词，描述水面之下的位置。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth-century diving, engineering and photography gave the word its modern technical compounds.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的潜水、工程与摄影赋予这个词现代的技术复合用法。

items.en: Late twentieth-century finance extended the word to debts larger than the asset behind them.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的金融把这个词扩展到超过抵押物价值的债务。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the compound's earliest citation is given differently in different dictionaries, though both elements are securely recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：复合词的最早书证各家词典所给年代不一，尽管两个成分记载可靠。

note.en: Group one holds the near-synonyms most often used in place of underwater; group two holds words for things that have gone beneath the surface.
note.cn: 第一组是常被用来替代 underwater 的近义词；第二组是描述已沉入水面之下的事物的词。

entries.definition: Beneath the sea, usually of the seabed, cables or volcanoes; it is narrower than underwater, which covers lakes and rivers too.
entries.definitionCN: 在海面之下，通常指海床、电缆或火山；比 underwater 窄，后者也涵盖湖泊与河流。

entries.definition: Below the sea surface, used chiefly in oil and gas engineering; it is a technical register, not a general word.
entries.definitionCN: 海面之下，主要用于油气工程；属技术语域，不是通用词。

entries.definition: The craft that dives, or an adjective for things beneath the sea; it does not describe ordinary underwater work.
entries.definitionCN: 指下潜的舰艇，或作形容词指海面之下的；不用于描述普通水下作业。

entries.definition: Completely covered by water, often after sinking or flooding; it stresses the event or state of being covered.
entries.definitionCN: 被水完全覆盖，常因沉没或淹没；强调被覆盖的事件或状态。

entries.definition: The literal phrase for position; it lacks the compact technical force of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 表示位置的字面短语；缺少复合词那种紧凑的技术力量。

entries.definition: Having sunk to the bottom; it describes a past event, whereas underwater only describes position.
entries.definitionCN: 已经沉到水底；描述过去事件，而 underwater 只描述位置。

entries.definition: Placed into a liquid, often for an experiment; it need not be a natural body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 放入液体中，常用于实验；不一定是自然水体。

entries.definition: Describing organisms that live in water, not the position of an object beneath the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 描述生活在水中的生物，不描述物体在水面下的位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real native words and real technical compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的本族词与真实的技术复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: under plus water is exactly below the surface: no hidden meaning.
normal.cn: under 加水就是水面之下：没有隐藏含义。

normal.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin: compare German Wasser and Dutch water.
normal.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语，不是拉丁语：可比德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: underwater camera, underwater pipeline, underwater archaeology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：水下相机、水下管道、水下考古。

normal.en: undersea is the seabed, underwater is the medium: the first is narrower.
normal.cn: undersea 指海床，underwater 指介质：前者更窄。

normal.en: The finance sense is a picture: a loan that cannot rise above the value of the house.
normal.cn: 金融义是一幅画：贷款浮不出房屋价值的水面。

abstract.en: Underwater is a room with a ceiling that moves.
abstract.cn: 水下是一个天花板会动的房间。

abstract.en: Light comes down as a permission, not as a fact.
abstract.cn: 光是在那里以一种许可的方式落下，而不是作为一种事实。

abstract.en: To be underwater in money is to breathe but not rise.
abstract.cn: 在钱上「在水下」，就是还能呼吸却浮不起来。

examples.en: The tunnel runs underwater for three kilometres.
examples.cn: 这条隧道在水下延伸三公里。

examples.en: Underwater robots inspect the pipeline every year.
examples.cn: 水下机器人每年检查这条管道。

examples.en: The diver stayed underwater for forty minutes.
examples.cn: 潜水员在水下停留了四十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: under（在下）+ water（水）＝水下的；位置在水面之下，也可指水下作业与设施，金融里比喻「浮不出水面」。

root: 古英语 under「在下方」+ 古英语 wæter「水」构成的英语复合词；属日耳曼语族，无拉丁语源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position: the place below the surface, its conditions, action done there, structures built there, imaging, life, a financial metaphor and submerged heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个位置展开：水面之下、那里的条件、在那里完成的动作、建在那里的设施、影像、生命、金融比喻与淹没的遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ceiling of water above, dim light leaking through it, blue in every direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶是一层水做的天花板，光从中漏下，四面皆蓝。

branches.en: PLACE AND CONDITIONS: below the surface, then the light and pressure found there.
branches.cn: 位置与条件：先是水面之下，再是那里的光与压力。

branches.en: ACTION AND BUILDING: doing work down there, then leaving structures there.
branches.cn: 动作与建造：先是在下面作业，再是在那里留下设施。

branches.en: SEEING AND LIVING: cameras record it, organisms inhabit it.
branches.cn: 看与生：相机记录它，生物栖息其中。

branches.en: DEBT BELOW THE LINE: unable to rise above what is owed.
branches.cn: 线下债务：无法浮到欠款之上。

branches.en: HERITAGE: what sank is preserved and studied.
branches.cn: 遗产：沉下去的东西被保存并被研究。

intro.en: Underwater is a transparent compound of two free English morphemes; no affix is involved, and each half can stand alone.
intro.cn: underwater 是两个自由英语语素的透明复合词，不涉及词缀，两半都能独立成词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, so there are no Latin entries. Latin sub 'under' and aqua 'water' express similar ideas from unrelated roots.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都属日耳曼语，因此没有拉丁条目。拉丁 sub「在下」与 aqua「水」用无关词根表达类似概念。

items.example: The rock lay under the boat.
items.exampleCN: 岩石在船下。

items.example: Water filled the basin.
items.exampleCN: 水注满了盆。

items.example: Underwater light turns blue with depth.
items.exampleCN: 水下光线随深度变蓝。

items.meaning: beneath the sea, especially the seabed
items.example: Undersea cables connect the continents.
items.exampleCN: 海底电缆连接各大陆。

items.meaning: below the sea, in engineering use
items.example: Subsea equipment sits on the wellhead.
items.exampleCN: 海底设备装在井口上。

items.example: The submerged reef lies two metres down.
items.exampleCN: 被淹没的礁在水下两米。

items.meaning: a camera sealed for use below water
items.meaningCN: 密封供水下使用的相机
items.example: The underwater camera filmed the reef.
items.exampleCN: 水下相机拍摄了礁体。

items.meaning: a pipe laid below the water surface
items.example: The underwater pipeline carries gas.
items.exampleCN: 水下管道输送天然气。

items.example: Underwater archaeology mapped the old harbour.
items.exampleCN: 水下考古测绘了旧港湾。

definition_zh: 潜艇；海面之下的（作名词指潜艇，作形容词指水下的、海底的）
definition_en: a warship that can travel under the sea; also an adjective meaning beneath the sea
core_image: 一艘细长的黑色艇体沉入水中，只留潜望镜划开水面，四周立刻安静下来
scene: 潜艇在洋脊旁缓缓下潜，螺旋桨搅起细小的气泡。The submarine dived quietly beside the research ship.
sceneCN: 这里 submarine 指「可潜航的舰艇」（第 1 个义项：作为船只的潜艇）；句意为这艘潜艇在考察船旁悄然下潜。

pos.zh: 海面之下的；海底的（多作定语，如 submarine cable、submarine canyon）

collocations.zh: 潜艇三明治（长条夹心面包）

derivatives.zh: submarine + -er（从事者后缀）→ 潜艇艇员：在潜艇上服役的人
sub-（在下）+ mergere（拉丁「沉入」）+ -sion（名词后缀）→ 浸没、下潜：沉入水下的动作或状态
sub- + mergere + -ible（能……的）→ 可潜航器；能潜入水下的
submarine（潜艇）+ sandwich（三明治）→ 潜艇三明治：形似艇体的长条夹心面包
anti-（希腊「对抗」）+ submarine（潜艇）→ 反潜的：用于对付潜艇的

senses.title: A diving warship
senses.definition: a vessel designed to operate beneath the surface
senses.definitionCN: 设计为在水面之下运作的船只
senses.example: The submarine dived quietly beside the research ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘潜艇在考察船旁悄然下潜。
senses.why: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea' literally means 'undersea', and the noun applies that to a craft.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」字面就是「海下」，名词把这个意思用在船只上。

senses.title: The submarine force
senses.definition: the branch of a navy that operates submarines, or its crews
senses.definitionCN: 海军中运作潜艇的兵种，或指其艇员
senses.example: Submarine crews train for months before deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 潜艇艇员在部署前训练数月。
senses.why: a fleet branch is named by its main equipment, so the word also stands for the service.
senses.whyCN: 兵种常以主要装备命名，因此这个词也代表该兵种。

senses.title: Beneath the sea, as an adjective
senses.definition: existing or occurring below the sea surface
senses.definitionCN: 存在于海面之下或发生在海面之下
senses.example: Submarine cables carry most international internet traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 海底电缆承载大部分国际互联网流量。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the literal sense of the Latin parts and attaches to whatever lies under the sea.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留拉丁成分的字面义，附在任何位于海面之下的事物上。

senses.title: Seafloor geology
senses.definition: the adjective used for canyons, fans and ridges on the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 用于海床上的峡谷、扇体与洋脊的形容词
senses.example: The submarine canyon feeds a fan of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海底峡谷养出一片砂质扇体。
senses.why: geology needed a short modifier for features hidden under water, and reused the existing adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个简短限定词来指藏在海水之下的地貌，于是复用了现成的形容词。

senses.title: Submarine cable engineering
senses.definition: the adjective for cables, pipes and structures laid on the seabed
senses.definitionCN: 用于铺设在海床上的电缆、管道与结构的形容词
senses.example: A submarine cable links the island to the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆把该岛与大陆相连。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed the adjective to installed infrastructure rather than ships.
senses.whyCN: 工程义把这个形容词收窄到已安装的基础设施，而非船只。

senses.title: The long sandwich
senses.titleCN: 潜艇三明治：长条夹心面包
senses.definition: a long roll split and filled, named for its shape
senses.definitionCN: 剖开夹馅的长条面包，因形状得名
senses.example: He ordered a submarine with cheese and ham.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一份夹奶酪与火腿的潜艇三明治。
senses.why: a long filled roll resembles a hull, so American English borrowed the vessel's name for the food.
senses.whyCN: 长条夹馅面包形似艇体，因此美式英语借船名来称这种食物。

senses.title: The underhand pitch
senses.definition: a baseball pitch delivered with the arm below the shoulder
senses.definitionCN: 手臂低于肩部投出的棒球球路
senses.example: The reliever throws with a submarine motion.
senses.exampleCN: 这名后援投手以下手动作投球。
senses.why: the low arm slot is figuratively beneath the usual plane, so baseball borrowed the sea word.
senses.whyCN: 低臂位在通常平面之下，因此棒球借用了这个海词。

senses.title: Hidden and silent action
senses.definition: the quality of moving unseen and unheard, as a submarine does
senses.definitionCN: 像潜艇那样不被看见、不被听见地行动
senses.example: The campaign ran like a submarine, silent until it surfaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这场行动像潜艇一样，一直无声，直到浮出水面。
senses.why: a submarine's military value is invisibility, so the word became a metaphor for concealed action.
senses.whyCN: 潜艇的军事价值在于不可见，因此这个词成为隐蔽行动的隐喻。

intro.en: Submarine is Latin in its parts: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. It entered English as an adjective in the seventeenth century and became a noun for the vessel at the end of the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: submarine 的各成分都是拉丁语：sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」，后者来自 mare「海」。它于十七世纪以形容词进入英语，到十九世纪末成为指舰船的名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and is the prefix in submerge, subsoil and submarine.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，是 submerge、subsoil 与 submarine 的前缀。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', the source of the -marine part.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，即 -marine 部分的来源。

items.en: Submarine first described things living or lying beneath the sea, not ships.
items.cn: submarine 最初描述生活在海面之下或位于海面之下的事物，并非船只。

items.en: Experimental submarines appeared in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, but the noun submarine for a warship settled in English around 1900.
items.cn: 实验性潜水器在十七、十八世纪出现，但指军舰的名词 submarine 约于一九零零年在英语中定型。

items.en: Two world wars made submarine a common word for the warship, and engineering extended it to cables and geology.
items.cn: 两次世界大战使 submarine 成为军舰的常用词，工程又把它扩展到电缆与地质。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): dates for the first noun use vary between 1899 and the early 1900s, and no single citation is universally accepted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：名词首次使用的年代在各家著作中自一八九九年至二十世纪初不等，没有公认的唯一书证。

note.en: Group one holds the vessels and craft most often confused with a submarine; group two holds the adjectives for things beneath the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是常与潜艇混淆的船只与潜器；第二组是表示海面之下的形容词。

entries.definition: A small craft carried by a ship and used for research or repair; it usually has no long-range independent patrol.
entries.definitionCN: 由母船携带、用于研究或修理的小型潜器；通常不能独立远航巡逻。

entries.definition: A person who works or swims underwater; it is human, not a vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 在水下工作或游泳的人；是人，不是船。

entries.definition: Any naval vessel built for combat; a submarine is one kind of warship, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 任何为作战建造的海军舰船；潜艇是军舰的一种，不是总称。

entries.definition: A long filled roll named for its hull-like shape; it has no connection to naval vessels beyond the metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 因形似艇体而得名的长条夹馅面包；除比喻外与军舰无关。

entries.definition: Beneath the sea, used of the seabed and its features; it is an adjective and cannot name the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 海面之下，用于海床及其地貌；只是形容词，不能命名舰船。

entries.definition: Below the surface of any water, fresh or salt; it is broader and not naval.
entries.definitionCN: 任何水体表面之下，淡水或咸水；范围更宽，且非海军用语。

entries.definition: Living or occurring partly under water; it is biological and rare, not a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 部分在水下生活或发生的；属生物学用语且罕见，不指船只。

entries.definition: Covered by water, often after sinking; a submarine is submerged by design, but the adjective alone implies no crew or engine.
entries.definitionCN: 被水覆盖，常因沉没；潜艇是设计上被淹没，但单用该形容词不暗示船员或动力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real naval and technical compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实的海军与技术复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub means under, mare means sea: the boat and the adjective say the same thing.
normal.cn: sub 是在下，mare 是海：船与形容词说的是同一件事。

normal.en: The adjective came first, the vessel noun came last: 1620s then about 1900.
normal.cn: 形容词先来，船只名词后到：十七世纪二十年代，再到约一九零零年。

normal.en: Fixed compounds split the senses: submarine cable is engineering, submarine canyon is geology.
normal.cn: 固定复合词分开义项：submarine cable 是工程，submarine canyon 是地质。

normal.en: The sandwich is named by shape, not by navy: a long roll like a hull.
normal.cn: 三明治按形状得名，与海军无关：长条面包像艇体。

normal.en: A submarine's weapon is silence: it is dangerous because it cannot be seen.
normal.cn: 潜艇的武器是沉默：它危险正因为看不见。

abstract.en: A submarine is a room that agrees to be forgotten.
abstract.cn: 潜艇是一间同意被遗忘的房间。

abstract.en: It moves through the sea the way a thought moves through silence.
abstract.cn: 它在海里移动，像念头在沉默中移动。

abstract.en: Its power is not speed but the absence of a surface.
abstract.cn: 它的力量不在速度，而在于没有表面。

examples.en: The submarine surfaced after a sixty-day patrol.
examples.cn: 这艘潜艇在六十天巡逻后浮出水面。

examples.en: Submarine cables carry data across the Atlantic.
examples.cn: 海底电缆跨大西洋传输数据。

examples.en: The museum displays a submarine from the last century.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出一艘上个世纪的潜艇。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub（在下）+ marine（海的）＝海面之下的；作名词就是潜艇，作形容词用于海底电缆、海底峡谷。

root: 拉丁 sub-「在下」+ marinus「海的」（源自 mare「海」）；十七世纪作形容词，十九世纪末作潜艇名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one craft and one position: the vessel, its service, the undersea adjective, seafloor geology, cables, the sandwich, the low pitch and the metaphor of silent concealment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一艘船与一个位置展开：舰艇、兵种、海下形容词、海底地质、电缆、三明治、低手投球，以及无声隐蔽的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long dark hull sliding under the surface until only a periscope remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：细长的深色艇体滑入水下，只剩潜望镜露在外面。

branches.en: CRAFT AND SERVICE: the vessel itself, then the branch that sails it.
branches.cn: 船与兵种：先是舰艇本身，再是运作它的兵种。

branches.en: THE UNDERSEA ADJECTIVE: position, seafloor geology, installed infrastructure.
branches.cn: 海下形容词：位置、海底地质、已安装设施。

branches.en: SHAPE METAPHOR: a long roll borrows the hull's name.
branches.cn: 形状比喻：长条面包借用了艇体的名字。

branches.en: LOW ARM SLOT: the pitch comes from beneath the usual plane.
branches.cn: 低臂位：球从通常平面之下投出。

branches.en: SILENT CONCEALMENT: invisibility becomes the point of the word.
branches.cn: 无声隐蔽：不可见成为这个词的要点。

intro.en: Submarine is a Latin prefix plus a Latin adjective, both still readable, and the English word inherits the full morphological structure.
intro.cn: submarine 是拉丁前缀加拉丁形容词，两者至今可读，英语词继承了完整的构词结构。

latinIntro.en: Sub- and marinus are the Latin entries; mare is the noun behind marinus. Together they spell 'under the sea'.
latinIntro.cn: sub- 与 marinus 是拉丁条目；mare 是 marinus 背后的名词。二者合起来就是「海之下」。

items.example: Sub- opens submerge and submarine.
items.exampleCN: sub- 开启 submerge 与 submarine。

items.example: Mare is the sea in Latin.
items.exampleCN: mare 是拉丁语的「海」。

items.example: Marinus gives the -marine of submarine.
items.exampleCN: marinus 给出 submarine 的 -marine 部分。

items.example: The submarine left the harbour at night.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇夜间离开港口。

items.meaning: a crew member of a submarine
items.example: The submariner served six years.
items.exampleCN: 这名艇员服役六年。

items.example: The tide submerges the rock.
items.exampleCN: 潮水淹没那块岩石。

items.meaning: able to go under water; a small craft
items.meaningCN: 能潜入水下的；小型潜器
items.example: The submersible surveyed the wreck.
items.exampleCN: 潜器勘察了沉船。

items.meaning: the act of putting under water
items.example: Submersion damaged the electronics.
items.exampleCN: 浸水损坏了电子设备。

items.meaning: a cable laid on the seabed
items.example: The submarine cable came ashore at the bay.
items.exampleCN: 海底电缆在海湾上岸。

items.example: The frigate ran an antisubmarine patrol.
items.exampleCN: 护卫舰执行了一次反潜巡逻。

definition_zh: 浮力；浮性；浮力大小；（情绪的）乐观；（经济的）回弹力
definition_en: the upward force that a fluid exerts on a body, or the quality of staying afloat and of remaining cheerful under pressure
core_image: 救生衣鼓满空气，落水的人被一股向上的力量托住，头始终露在水面
scene: 救生衣鼓满空气，落水者的头始终露在水面上。A life jacket gives a swimmer enough buoyancy to stay afloat.
sceneCN: 这里 buoyancy 指「流体对物体产生的向上托举力」（第 1 个义项：物理浮力）；句意为救生衣给游泳者足够的浮力使其保持漂浮。

pos.zh: 浮力；浮性；乐观；回弹力（不可数，复数 buoyancies 较少用）

derivatives.zh: buoy（中古荷兰语 boeye「浮标」，可能与拉丁 boia「皮制颈环」有关但未证实）→ 浮标；使浮起、鼓舞
buoy + -ant（拉丁 -antem，表性质的形容词后缀）→ 有浮力的；轻快的、乐观的
buoyant + -ly（副词后缀）→ 轻快地；乐观地
buoyancy + aid（辅助物）→ 助浮具：帮助人漂浮的装备
buoyancy + compensator（补偿器）→ 浮力补偿装置：潜水员用来调节浮力的背心

senses.title: The upward force of a fluid
senses.definition: the upward force exerted by a liquid or gas on a body in it
senses.definitionCN: 液体或气体对其中的物体施加的向上力量
senses.example: A life jacket gives a swimmer enough buoyancy to stay afloat.
senses.exampleCN: 救生衣给游泳者足够的浮力使其保持漂浮。
senses.why: a submerged body displaces fluid, and the displaced fluid pushes back upward; that push is the buoyancy.
senses.whyCN: 浸入的物体排开流体，被排开的流体向上回推，这一推力就是浮力。

senses.title: The quality of staying afloat
senses.titleCN: 浮性：物体保持漂浮的性质
senses.definition: the property of an object that keeps it on or near the surface
senses.definitionCN: 使物体留在水面或接近水面的性质
senses.example: The buoyancy of the hull depends on trapped air.
senses.exampleCN: 船体的浮性取决于内部封存的空气。
senses.why: the force and the property are two sides of one fact: what the fluid does, and what the object can rely on.
senses.whyCN: 力与性质是同一事实的两面：流体做了什么，以及物体能依靠什么。

senses.title: A measured amount
senses.definition: the magnitude of the upward force, often expressed as a reserve
senses.definitionCN: 向上力量的大小，常以储备量表示
senses.example: Divers adjust their buoyancy at every depth.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在每个深度都调整浮力。
senses.why: engineering needs a number, so buoyancy becomes a quantity to calculate and control.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要一个数，因此浮力成为可计算、可控制的量。

senses.title: Lightness of mood
senses.definition: a cheerful, light-hearted feeling
senses.definitionCN: 愉快、轻松的心情
senses.example: The buoyancy of the crowd lifted the whole evening.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的轻快情绪点亮了整个夜晚。
senses.why: something buoyant rides high rather than sinking, and moods are described with the same up-down geometry.
senses.whyCN: 有浮力的东西浮在高处而不下沉，心情也用同一套上下几何来描述。

senses.title: Resilience under pressure
senses.definition: the ability to recover quickly from difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 从困难中迅速恢复的能力
senses.example: Her buoyancy surprised everyone after the setback.
senses.exampleCN: 遭遇挫折后，她的韧性让所有人惊讶。
senses.why: what is buoyant comes back to the surface after being pushed down, which is the shape of resilience.
senses.whyCN: 有浮力的东西被压下去后会回到水面，这正是韧性的形状。

senses.title: Market or economic lift
senses.definition: the tendency of prices or activity to stay firm or recover
senses.definitionCN: 价格或经济活动保持坚挺或回升的倾向
senses.example: Analysts noted the buoyancy of the housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师注意到住房市场的回弹力。
senses.why: economists borrowed the float-and-recover image to describe prices that refuse to sink.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借「浮起与回弹」的意象，描述拒绝下沉的价格。

senses.title: Rising fluid in convection
senses.definition: the tendency of warm, less dense fluid to rise
senses.definitionCN: 较暖、密度较小的流体上升的倾向
senses.example: Thermal buoyancy drives the plume upward.
senses.exampleCN: 热浮力把羽流向上驱动。
senses.why: the same physical rule applies to air and water: lighter fluid rises through heavier fluid.
senses.whyCN: 同一条物理规则适用于空气与水：较轻的流体穿过较重的流体上升。

senses.title: Reserve lift in a vessel
senses.definition: the unused lifting capacity above a vessel's working waterline
senses.definitionCN: 船舶工作水线以上尚未使用的托举能力
senses.example: The ship's buoyancy reserve kept it afloat with one flooded compartment.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船的储备浮力使它在进水一个舱室后仍能漂浮。
senses.why: safety engineering counts not total lift but the unused margin, so buoyancy also names that margin.
senses.whyCN: 安全工程计的不是总托举力，而是未用的余量，因此浮力也命名那份余量。

intro.en: Buoyancy is formed in English from buoy plus the Latin-derived noun suffix -ancy, from -antia. The origin of buoy itself is unsettled: it came through Middle Dutch or Old French, and a link to Latin boia 'leather collar' is only a hypothesis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: buoyancy 在英语中由 buoy 加拉丁语源名词后缀 -ancy（来自 -antia）构成。buoy 本身的来源没有定论：它经中古荷兰语或古法语而来，与拉丁 boia「皮制颈环」的联系只是假说。年代均为约数。

items.en: Buoy appears in English in the sixteenth century, probably from Middle Dutch boeye or Old French buie, both meaning a float or a fetter.
items.cn: buoy 于十六世纪出现在英语中，可能来自中古荷兰语 boeye 或古法语 buie，两者都指浮标或束缚物。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-English origin of buoy is not agreed. The suggestion that it goes back to Latin boia 'a leather collar' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：buoy 在英语之前的来源没有共识。认为它上溯拉丁 boia「皮制颈环」的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The noun suffix -ancy comes from Latin -antia, which forms abstract nouns of state or quality.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ancy 来自拉丁 -antia，用于构成表示状态或性质的抽象名词。

items.en: The noun buoyancy appears in the early eighteenth century, first for the physical tendency to float.
items.cn: 名词 buoyancy 于十八世纪初出现，最初指物理上的漂浮倾向。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word described cheerful spirits, and in the twentieth it was applied to markets and economies.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词描述愉快的情绪；到二十世纪，它被用于市场与经济。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): references give slightly different years for the first use of buoyancy, and no single citation is authoritative.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各工具书对 buoyancy 首次使用的年份略有出入，没有权威的唯一书证。

note.en: Group one holds the physics terms most often confused with buoyancy; group two holds the figurative words for lift and cheer.
note.cn: 第一组是常与浮力混淆的物理术语；第二组是表示托举与振奋的比喻词。

entries.definition: Describing something that floats or someone cheerful; buoyancy is the force or quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述会漂浮的物体或开朗的人；buoyancy 是力或性质本身。

entries.definition: Mass per unit volume; it decides whether an object floats, but it is not the upward force.
entries.definitionCN: 单位体积的质量；它决定物体是否漂浮，但不是向上的力。

entries.definition: The volume of fluid pushed aside by a body; buoyancy is the force that displaced fluid produces.
entries.definitionCN: 物体排开的流体体积；浮力是这些被排开流体产生的力。

entries.definition: To rest on a liquid surface; it describes the behaviour, while buoyancy names the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 停在液面上；描述行为，而 buoyancy 命名原因。

entries.definition: An upward force, especially on a wing; buoyancy is the fluid-resting case of the same direction.
entries.definitionCN: 向上的力，尤指机翼上的升力；浮力是同一方向的流体静置情形。

entries.definition: The ability to recover shape or spirit after pressure; it overlaps with the figurative buoyancy of mood.
entries.definitionCN: 受压后恢复形状或精神的能力；与情绪义的 buoyancy 重叠。

entries.definition: The state of being happy and pleasant; it is the everyday equivalent of the mood sense.
entries.definitionCN: 愉快而开朗的状态；是情绪义项的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The ability of a material to return to its original form; it is physical, not fluid lift.
entries.definitionCN: 材料恢复原状的能力；属材料物理，而非流体托举。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real physics, real suffixes and real economic metaphors, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的物理、真实的后缀与真实的经济比喻，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Archimedes in one line: the water pushes up as hard as the water that was pushed aside.
normal.cn: 阿基米德一句话：水向上推的力，等于被排开的水。

normal.en: Three states in diving: positive, neutral and negative buoyancy.
normal.cn: 潜水三态：正浮力、中性浮力、负浮力。

normal.en: -ancy is a state suffix, like -ance in resistance: buoyancy is the state of being buoyant.
normal.cn: -ancy 是状态后缀，如 resistance 的 -ance：buoyancy 就是处于 buoyant 的状态。

normal.en: The metaphor is geometry: what floats comes back up after being pushed down.
normal.cn: 比喻是几何的：浮得起的东西被压下后会回到上面。

normal.en: Markets borrow the word when prices refuse to sink.
normal.cn: 价格拒绝下沉时，市场就借用了这个词。

abstract.en: Buoyancy is the water's polite refusal to let you disappear.
abstract.cn: 浮力是水礼貌地拒绝让你消失。

abstract.en: It is an argument between weight and volume, settled upward.
abstract.cn: 它是重量与体积之间的一场争论，结论朝上。

abstract.en: A cheerful person carries private buoyancy no one can measure.
abstract.cn: 开朗的人带着别人无法测量的私人浮力。

examples.en: The submarine adjusts buoyancy by flooding and emptying tanks.
examples.cn: 潜艇通过注水和排空水舱来调整浮力。

examples.en: Warm water rises because of its buoyancy.
examples.cn: 暖水因浮力而上升。

examples.en: The market showed unexpected buoyancy in the spring.
examples.cn: 市场在春季表现出意外的回弹力。

dict_mnemonic.text: buoy（浮标）+ -ancy（状态）＝浮着的状态；物理上是排开流体换来的向上托力，引申为心情轻快与经济回弹。

root: buoy（中古荷兰语 boeye 或古法语 buie「浮标、束缚物」，更早来源不确定）+ 拉丁 -antia 名词后缀 -ancy；十八世纪初出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upward push: the fluid force, the property of floating, its measured amount, light mood, resilience, market lift, convection and a ship's reserve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股向上推力展开：流体力、漂浮性质、可测的量、轻快心情、韧性、市场回弹、对流上升，以及船舶储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body held at the surface by water pushing up harder than gravity pulls down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个物体被水托在水面，因为向上的推力大于向下的重力。

branches.en: PHYSICS: the force, its measured value and the unused safety margin.
branches.cn: 物理：力本身、它的量值，以及未用的安全余量。

branches.en: PROPERTY: what an object can rely on to stay up.
branches.cn: 性质：物体可以依靠它留在上面的特性。

branches.en: MOOD: lightness and the ability to come back up.
branches.cn: 心情：轻快，以及回到上面的能力。

branches.en: MARKET: prices that refuse to sink.
branches.cn: 市场：拒绝下沉的价格。

branches.en: CONVECTION: warm fluid rising through cold.
branches.cn: 对流：暖流体穿过冷流体上升。

intro.en: Buoyancy is a transparent English derivation: a borrowed noun stem plus a Latin abstract suffix.
intro.cn: buoyancy 是透明的英语派生：借入的名词词干加拉丁抽象后缀。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -antia is the Latin entry. Buoy itself has no established Latin ancestor, so the possible link to boia is not listed as an entry.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -antia 是拉丁条目。buoy 本身没有已确立的拉丁祖先，因此与 boia 的可能联系不列为条目。
